title: Agent Host Copilot harness treats denied client tool options as approved
description:
## Issue

In the **Agent Host Copilot harness** (not the Local harness), browser-tool confirmation choices are not honored correctly.

## Repro: Skip

1. Close all open Integrated Browser tabs.
2. Start a Copilot session using the **Agent Host Copilot harness**, not the Local harness.
3. Ask Copilot: `Please open Wikipedia.`
4. When asked for permission to open the page, choose **Skip**.

**Actual:** Copilot proceeds with the browser action even though **Skip** was selected.

**Expected:** The browser action is cancelled and no page is opened.

## Repro: Allow in Session

1. Close all open Integrated Browser tabs.
2. Start a Copilot session using the **Agent Host Copilot harness**, not the Local harness.
3. Ask Copilot: `Please open Wikipedia.`
4. When asked for permission to open the page, choose **Allow in Session**.
5. Close the Wikipedia tab that just opened
6. In the same session, ask Copilot: `Please open Bing.`
**Actual:** Copilot asks for permission again.

**Expected:** Copilot remembers the permission for the session and opens the page without prompting again.
label: bug

title: Scope "Auto accept delay" and "Select a code block" tips to normal/editor windows (not Agents)
description:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: (unknown)
- VS Code Version: (all / please specify if you can reproduce on Insiders)
- OS Version: (all)
- Feature: Copilot Chat tips shown in Agents vs normal editor/new-chat windows
- Selected model: n/a
- Logs: N/A (attach logs if available)

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open the Agents window in VS Code (Copilot Chat Agents view).
2. Observe that tips such as “Auto accept delay” and “Select a code block” are displayed.
3. Open a normal editor or new-chat window and observe the same tips appearing there as well.
4. Note the inconsistency: these tips feel editor/new-chat specific but are showing in Agents.

Expected behavior / Acceptance criteria:
- The "Auto accept delay" and "Select a code block" tips should be scoped to editor/new-chat (normal) windows only and should not appear in the Agents window.
- Tips that are editor-specific should only surface where they are relevant to avoid UI clutter in Agents.
- Dismiss/reset behavior should remain consistent (document whether dismissals are global or per-window).

Additional notes:
- Users in Slack reported seeing these tips in new chat, editor windows, and vscode.dev; some users do not see them in Agents consistently. Consider platform-specific behavior and feature-flagging/telemetry when investigating.

title: Toolbar commands immediately close newly opened quick picks
description:
### Type of Bug

Regression

### Reproduction

1. Run a current VS Code Insiders build with the modern UI/style override and motion enabled.
2. Open Source Control.
3. Open a toolbar **More Actions...** menu for a repository.
4. Open **Branch** and invoke **Create Branch From...**.
5. Observe the quick pick.

This also reproduces with other commands invoked from workbench toolbars that open a quick pick. Invoking the same commands from the Command Center does not reproduce the problem.

### Expected Behavior

The command's quick pick remains open and focused.

### Actual Behavior

The Command Center/quick-pick surface briefly opens, then immediately closes and focus returns to the toolbar menu.

### Regression Details

The regression was introduced by c5f02db50896ef310d3c909628e651675644fcef ("Add open/close motion to button menus in workbench chrome", #325190).

Animated context views delay disposal for the close animation. During that interval, the closing toolbar menu remains focusable. Its existing mouse-out handling can focus the menu's `actions-container` after the command has opened and focused a quick pick. The quick pick then receives a blur event and closes.

The issue only appears when the context-view close animation is active, which explains why it reproduces on machines enrolled in the modern UI/style override but not necessarily on every machine running the same Insiders version.

### VS Code Version

Current VS Code Insiders (1.133 development cycle); regression is also present on the 1.132 release branch.

title: Speech-to-text fails with NotAllowedError: Permission denied in auxiliary (floating) chat windows
description:
Type: Bug Microphone / speech-to-text works correctly in the main VS Code window, but fails immediately when the same chat is opened in an auxiliary (floating) window. Steps to reproduce: Open a Copilot Chat in the main VS Code window. Start speech-to-text (dictation) — works fine. Right-click the chat → Move into New Window (auxiliary window). Start speech-to-text in the floating window. An error appears at the bottom of the window: Expected: Microphone permission granted to the session should apply to auxiliary windows, so speech-to-text works there too. Actual: getUserMedia is rejected with NotAllowedError: Permission denied in the auxiliary window only. The main window continues to work. Regression: This started ~2–3 days ago after a VS Code update. It was not an issue before. Notes / observations: Only auxiliary/floating windows are affected; docked chat in the primary window works. Windows OS-level microphone permission is enabled for desktop apps (main window confirms the mic is accessible). Appears to be that the auxiliary window is a separate Chromium browser context and does not inherit the microphone permission grant from the primary window. title: Require confirmation for CMD delayed-expansion redirect destinations
description:
Terminal auto-approval can treat a file redirect destination containing balanced CMD delayed environment-variable expansion, such as `!VARIABLE!\file.txt`, as a literal path relative to the terminal working directory.

The final destination is resolved later by CMD when delayed expansion is enabled, so the pre-expansion text is not authoritative for workspace containment.

Expected behavior:

- Recognize balanced, non-empty CMD delayed-expansion syntax in redirect destinations.
- Require the normal terminal confirmation instead of classifying the target as workspace-local.
- Keep ordinary or unmatched `!` characters eligible for auto-approval.
- Apply the same destination-safety behavior in workbench and Agent Host terminal permission checks.
- Preserve existing Bash, PowerShell, literal-path, and file-write setting behavior.

Implementation: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/329055

title: Terminal auto-approval allows git show file output without confirmation
description:
## Problem

Terminal auto-approval treats `git show` as a read-only command, but `git show` can write directly to a file through its `--output` option:

```bash
git show --format=%B --output=message.txt HEAD
git show --output message.txt HEAD
```

Because `--output` is a Git option rather than a shell redirect, it does not produce a tree-sitter `file_redirect` node. The write-destination check is therefore not consulted, and the command can be auto-approved.

The existing default rules already require confirmation for `git log --output`, but not for the equivalent `git show` option.

## Expected

- `git show --output=<path>` and `git show --output <path>` require confirmation in both workbench and Agent Host terminal auto-approval.
- Plain `git show`, `git show --format=...`, and similarly named options remain auto-approved.
- Workbench and Agent Host use the same default Git rule definitions.

title: Session creation pill is hidden in completed work summary
description: ## Steps to Reproduce 1. Open the Agents window and start a session. 2. Ask the agent to perform multiple steps and create a tracked session with `create_session` or `create_chat`. 3. Wait for the response to complete and collapse into the **Completed N steps** summary. ## Actual Result The created-session or created-chat pill is moved into the collapsed work summary, hiding the durable navigation affordance until the summary is expanded. ## Expected Result The created-session or created-chat pill remains visible with the final response summary at the bottom, alongside other completed-turn adjuncts. ## Verification 1. Repeat the reproduction prompt and wait for the turn to complete. 2. Confirm **Completed N steps** contains only the work performed before the final response. 3. Confirm the session/chat pill appears below the final response and remains visible while the work summary is collapsed. 4. Activate the pill with the mouse and keyboard and confirm it opens the created session/chat. ## Screenshot

title: Agent Host auto-approves sed in-place edits
description:
## Problem

Agent Host's terminal auto-approval rules allow normal `sed` commands, but do not distinguish in-place editing forms such as:

```bash
sed -i 's/foo/bar/' file.txt
sed --in-place 's/foo/bar/' file.txt
```

These forms modify files through command arguments rather than shell redirects, so the existing redirect write check does not see them. As a result, a recognized `sed` command can be auto-approved even though it edits a file directly.

Workbench already detects canonical `sed` in-place forms through its command-specific file-write parser.

## Expected

- Agent Host should require confirmation for canonical `sed` in-place forms, including `-i`, `-I`, clustered/backup-suffix variants, BSD empty suffixes, and `--in-place`.
- A configured full-command allow rule should not override this check.
- Normal non-in-place `sed` commands should retain their existing auto-approval behavior.
- Workbench file-write behavior and settings should remain unchanged.

Broader shell-dialect and dynamic-option hardening is tracked separately in #328898.

title: Agent session continues in original repository when worktree creation fails due to missing Git LFS
description:
## Summary

When an Agents window session is configured to use worktree isolation, worktree creation can fail if `git-lfs` is unavailable to the Agent Host. The session nevertheless continues in the original repository, without the requested isolation.

## Observed behavior

The Agent Host attempted:

```text
git -c checkout.workers=0 worktree add --no-track -b agents/simple-test-setup-3cee819a /Users/justinq/Documents/GitHub/vscode.worktrees/simple-test-setup-3cee819a origin/main
```

Git failed with exit code 128:

```text
Preparing worktree (new branch 'agents/simple-test-setup-3cee819a')
git-lfs filter-process: git-lfs: command not found
fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly
```

The Agent Host logged:

```text
[AgentService] worktree resolution failed for copilotcli:/3cee819a-bbee-43db-a484-859dfbdfe4d2: git -c exited with code 128: git-lfs filter-process: git-lfs: command not found
```

Despite this failure, the session materialized and ran with:

```text
cwd: /Users/justinq/Documents/GitHub/vscode
gitRoot: /Users/justinq/Documents/GitHub/vscode
branch: main
```

The turn then completed successfully, but in the original checkout rather than the requested worktree. The same worktree failure occurred for another session one minute earlier, so this was reproducible in that environment.

There was also an earlier shell-environment resolution timeout:

```text
resolving shell environment failed Unable to resolve your shell environment in a reasonable time. Please review your shell configuration and restart.
```

This may explain why `git-lfs` was not on the Agent Host PATH, although Git LFS may also have been absent entirely.

## Expected behavior

If worktree isolation is requested and worktree creation fails, the session should not silently continue in the original repository. The failure should be surfaced clearly and the session should either stop or require explicit user confirmation before falling back.

The error should also identify the missing Git LFS executable and, where applicable, suggest checking Agent Host shell-environment/PATH resolution.

## Additional notes

Unrelated MCP startup and authentication errors appeared in the bundle but did not cause the worktree failure.

title: Agent Host can delete durable sessions after transient resume failures
description:
## Problem

An existing Agent Host session can disappear permanently after a transient Copilot SDK resume failure.

The SDK reports both genuinely empty sessions and unrelated failures with JSON-RPC code `-32603`. Agent Host treated nearly every `-32603` as an empty session and replaced the existing SDK session with a new empty session using the same ID.

When that zero-turn state later lost its final subscriber, empty-session GC treated it as an abandoned provisional draft and invoked destructive disposal. That deleted the SDK event history, Agent Host session database, and worktree.

## Expected

- Network, authentication, corruption, and unknown resume failures preserve all durable session data and surface the error.
- Empty-session recreation is limited to explicit SDK `no events` and `Session not found` responses.
- Destructive empty-session GC only applies to pristine provisional sessions that have never materialized or persisted data.
- Chat, changeset, and annotations subscriptions keep their owning session alive.

## Additional context

The issue was reproduced with session `f72992a0-b278-45e0-b094-4e78dd0b1370`. Its exported debug bundle retained 2,552 SDK events, including 10 user messages, immediately before Agent Host GC deleted the live session.

Fix: [#328540](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328540)

title: Terminal auto-approve overlooks shell state mutations before allowed commands
description:
## Problem

Terminal command auto-approval currently extracts only tree-sitter `(command)` nodes. Shell state mutations that are not captured as commands can sit in front of an allow-listed command and still get auto-approved.

Examples that should require confirmation:

```bash
export FOO=bar && git status
declare -x FOO=bar && git status
FOO=bar && git status
```

```powershell
$env:FOO="bar"; git status
[System.Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable("FOO", "bar"); git status
```

In these cases the approver sees only the trailing allow-listed command and can approve the whole line.

## Expected

- Any standalone Bash assignment/declaration or PowerShell assignment/invocation that mutates shell state should fail closed and require manual confirmation.
- Prefix assignments attached to a command (`FOO=bar git status`) should continue to use the existing transient env-var deny path.
- Ordinary command arguments that happen to look like `NAME=value` (for example `make install PREFIX=/usr/local`) should still be auto-approvable when the command itself is allowed.
- Auto-approve rule suggestions should not be offered for command lines containing this unanalyzable shell-state syntax.

## Notes

- Affects both workbench terminal auto-approval and Agent Host Bash approval.
- Agent Host PowerShell already fails closed on assignments and invocations; workbench should match that shape.

title: Standalone dictation mic button is too small when Voice Mode is not enabled
description: When Voice Mode is not enabled, the standalone dictation mic button renders too small compared to the surrounding execute-toolbar controls, making it look weightless and hard to target. This should be resolved by #328137, which makes the execute-toolbar controls a uniform set of 22px circular buttons and gives the standalone dictation / Voice Mode buttons their own circular ring. cc @meganrogge

title: Agent Host session can remain stuck on Working after config-driven refresh
description:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: N/A — this is the core Agents window / Agent Host Copilot CLI provider
- VS Code Version: 1.132.0-insider (`d1ced2b15b280d2cf7a77b12baafaf5e68f7076c`)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84)
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agents window, existing Copilot CLI Agent Host session, config-driven SDK session refresh
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol
- Logs: Sanitized excerpts below

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open an existing Copilot CLI session in the Agents window.
2. Change the active client tool/plugin configuration relative to the SDK session's applied snapshot. A window reload/reconnect can produce this state; the important condition is that `ActiveClient.requiresRestart(...)` returns `true` on the next send.
3. Have an unresolved guarded SDK callback on the old session, such as a permission, user-input, MCP-auth, elicitation, exit-plan, unsandboxed-command, or client-tool callback.
4. Send another prompt. `_sendMessage()` detects the changed configuration and awaits `CopilotAgentSession.destroySession()` before resuming the SDK session.
5. Observe that the session remains on **Working...**. Cancelling does not unblock it, and another prompt can receive a `chat/turnStarted` echo without any terminal `chat/turnComplete`, `chat/error`, or `chat/turnCancelled` action.

A deterministic code-level reproduction is:

1. Create a `CopilotAgentSession`.
2. Call a guarded runtime callback such as `runtime.handlePermissionRequest(...)` and leave it unresolved.
3. Call `session.destroySession()`.
4. Before the fix, `session.disconnect()` is reached while the callback is still pending. The real SDK can wait for that callback during disconnect, so `destroySession()` never settles.

## Actual result

The session card remains on **Working...** indefinitely. The per-session operation queue is blocked, so cancel, retry, release, and later sends cannot make progress.

## Expected result

Config-driven teardown must cancel all pending interactive/client callbacks before disconnecting. The old SDK session should disconnect, the refreshed session should resume, and the turn should either proceed or terminate with an explicit error.

## Sanitized log timeline

Agent Host log (local time):

```text
12:40:04.590 [Copilot:<session>] sendMessage: cachedEntry=true, hasActiveClient=true, activeClientId=(set)
12:40:04.593 [Copilot:<session>] Session config changed (requiresRestart=true), refreshing session

# The expected "No cached entry ..., calling _resumeSession" line never follows.

12:44:34.340 [AgentHost] Cancellation requested for <session>, dispatching turnCancelled
12:49:58.815 [AgentService] Restored session <session> with 18 turns
12:49:59.139 [Copilot:<session>] Clearing custom agent selection
12:49:59.140 Request session.agent.deselect failed: Session not found for sessionId: <session>
12:49:59.140 [AgentSideEffects] changeAgent failed: Session not found for sessionId: <session>
```

AHP log (UTC), for the later retry:

```text
10:49:59.137 c2s chat/turnStarted turnId=<turn>
10:49:59.140 s2c chat/turnStarted turnId=<turn>
# No terminal action for this turn follows.
```

## Root cause

`CopilotAgent._sendMessage()` runs under `_sessionSequencer.queue(sessionId, ...)`. When the current active-client snapshot differs from the SDK session's applied snapshot, it performs a config refresh by awaiting `entry.destroySession()` before clearing the default chat and calling `_resumeSession()`.

`CopilotAgentSession.dispose()` and `abort()` both call `_beginAbort()`. That cancellation path cancels the session token and resolves/rejects all pending guarded interactions through `_cancelAllPendingInteractions()`. `destroySession()`, however, only flushed edit attribution and awaited `this._wrapper.session.disconnect()`; it did not call `_beginAbort()` first.

If the SDK disconnect waits for one of those pending callbacks, `destroySession()` never resolves. Because this happens while `_sendMessage()` owns the per-session sequencer, all later operations for the same session queue behind it. The protocol has already accepted and echoed `chat/turnStarted`, so the UI shows an active turn, but no provider send or terminal action can run. Cancellation is also routed through the same sequencer and therefore cannot break the deadlock. The later `session.agent.deselect` "Session not found" error is a secondary symptom of continuing to address the torn-down SDK session.

## Proposed fix

Call `_beginAbort()` at the start of `CopilotAgentSession.destroySession()`, before edit-attribution flushing and SDK disconnect. This mirrors normal disposal semantics and deterministically settles every guarded callback before the disconnect begins.

Add a regression test that leaves a permission callback pending, calls `destroySession()`, and verifies from a disconnect hook that the callback has already resolved to `{ kind: 'reject' }` when SDK disconnect starts. This exercises the ordering that prevents the per-session sequencer deadlock.

- VS Code Version: 1.131.0
- OS Version: macOS

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure a BYOK model that supports reasoning effort (e.g. Anthropic Claude or OpenAI o-series) via the Copilot extension's BYOK settings
2. Enable `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled` in settings and restart the Agent Host process
3. Open an AgentHost Copilot session, open the model picker, and select the BYOK model
4. Observe: the thinking effort / reasoning effort configuration option is missing

**Expected:** The BYOK model in the AgentHost picker should expose the same reasoning effort configuration (e.g. Low / Medium / High) that is available in the regular Copilot Chat model picker.

**Actual:** The BYOK model shows in the picker but has no thinking effort selector. The same model shows the reasoning effort option correctly in the regular (non-AgentHost) Copilot Chat model picker.

## Root Cause

The BYOK bridge DTO (`IByokLmModelInfo`) between the renderer and the Agent Host process has never carried reasoning effort information. This is a gap in the bridge design, not a regression — the `configSchema` was simply never included when the model metadata DTO was incrementally built up.

**Data flow comparison:**

| Path | `configSchema` | Reasoning Effort |
|------|---------------|-----------------|
| CAPI models → `_listModels()` | ✅ `_createModelConfigSchema()` synthesizes `thinkingLevel` | ✅ |
| BYOK models → `_refreshByokModels()` | ❌ not set | ❌ |

The renderer-side `AgentHostByokLmHandler.listModels()` has access to `metadata.configurationSchema` (which includes `reasoningEffort` set by the Copilot extension's `byokModelInfo.ts`) but does not read or forward it. Consequently, `CopilotAgent._refreshByokModels()` cannot synthesize a `configSchema` for BYOK models, and `AgentHostLanguageModelProvider` receives `configSchema: undefined`.

## Proposed Fix

Three surgical changes thread reasoning effort through the bridge:

**1. `src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostByokLm.ts`** — add fields to `IByokLmModelInfo`:
```typescript
readonly supportsReasoningEffort?: readonly string[];

title: Agent Host session read/unread state is not synced between the editor window and the agents window
description:
Read/unread state for an Agent Host session is tracked separately by each surface, so the two windows disagree about whether a session has been read.

- The **agents window** already routes read state through the Agent Host: `ISession.isRead` is backed by the protocol `IsRead` status bit, which the host persists and fans out to connected clients.
- The **editor window** does not. `AgentSessionsModel` keeps its own read *timestamps* in `IStorageService`, with no path to or from the host.

The result: opening a session in one window leaves it showing as unread in the other, and a session the host marks unread after background output doesn't surface as unread in the editor window.

There is a second, related problem inside the host itself. Read state has two parallel representations — the `SessionStatus.IsRead` bit and standalone `isRead` / `isArchived` booleans on the local `IAgentSessionMetadata` IPC shape. Different code paths read different ones, and `listSessions()` could return the two disagreeing. Any fix needs one source of truth rather than a third consumer of an ambiguous pair.

This is host-owned rather than agent-owned, so it applies equally to Copilot, Claude, and Codex sessions — none of those SDKs track read state themselves.

## How to verify

1. Open a workspace and start an Agent Host session (Copilot, Claude, or Codex) from the agents window. Send a prompt and let the turn finish.
2. Leave the session **unread**: navigate away in the agents window without opening it after the turn completes. It should show an unread indicator.
3. Open the **editor window** (Chat Sessions view) for the same workspace and find that session in the list.
   - **Expected:** it shows as unread in both windows.
   - **Before the fix:** the two windows disagree.
4. Click the session in the editor window to open it, then switch back to the agents window.
   - **Expected:** it is now marked read in the agents window too, without a reload.
5. Do the reverse: right-click the session in the agents window → **Mark as Unread**, then check the editor window's list.
   - **Expected:** it shows as unread there as well.
6. With the session sitting idle and read, send it a message from one window and let the turn complete while the session is not being viewed.
   - **Expected:** both windows show it as unread once the turn finishes.

Reloading either window should preserve whatever the host last recorded, since the state is persisted host-side rather than in per-window storage.

Fixed by #327950.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Interrupted versioned user update can lose product target and install system setup
description:
﻿<!-- Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A

- VS Code Version: 1.131.0-insider (user setup)
- OS Version: Windows 11 x64 10.0.26200

## Summary

A versioned Windows User Setup contains two entries for `resources/app/product.json`:

1. The recursive `Source: "*"` entry copies the generic build `product.json`, which has no `target`.
2. A later explicit entry copies the setup-generated `product.json` containing `"target": "user"`.

If setup aborts after the first entry but before the second, rollback can leave the generic file in an existing version directory. The next VS Code process has `productService.target === undefined`, so it requests the system update feed and uses the foreground system setup flow. This can silently turn a user installation into parallel user and system installations.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install and launch an Insiders **User Setup** build that uses versioned Windows updates.
2. Keep the matching `VSCodeUserSetup-x64-<version>-insider.exe` available.
3. In PowerShell, exclusively hold a file that occurs after `product.json` in the recursive setup file list:

```powershell
$installDir = "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Programs\Microsoft VS Code Insiders"
$versionDir = Get-ChildItem $installDir -Directory |
    Where-Object Name -Match '^[0-9a-f]{10}$' |
    Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending |
    Select-Object -First 1
$lockedFile = Join-Path $versionDir.FullName 'resources\app\node_modules.asar.unpacked\@vscode\policy-watcher\build\Release\vscode-policy-watcher.node'
$stream = [IO.File]::Open($lockedFile, [IO.FileMode]::Open, [IO.FileAccess]::Read, [IO.FileShare]::Read)
```

4. Re-run the matching User Setup package using the update-style arguments:

```powershell
& .\VSCodeUserSetup-x64-<version>-insider.exe /verysilent /log /nocloseapplications '/mergetasks=runcode,!desktopicon,!quicklaunchicon'
```

5. When setup reports that it cannot replace `vscode-policy-watcher.node`, choose **Abort**, then release the handle:

```powershell
$stream.Dispose()
```

6. Inspect the installed product metadata:

```powershell
$product = Get-Content (Join-Path $versionDir.FullName 'resources\app\product.json') -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
$product.target
```

## Actual Result

`target` is missing. On the next available update:

- The cache directory is named `vscode-insider-undefined-x64`.
- Update metadata points to `VSCodeSetup-x64-...exe`, not `VSCodeUserSetup-x64-...exe`.
- Setup runs with `/silent` and creates an HKLM installation under `C:\Program Files\Microsoft VS Code Insiders` alongside the existing user installation.

The setup log for the aborted update contains one generic `product.json` write before the locked-file error. A successful setup normally contains a second `product.json` write with the target-specific generated file.

## Expected Result

A User Setup package must never install a generic `product.json`. Its only `product.json` payload should always contain `"target": "user"`, including after cancellation, failure, or rollback.

## Root Cause

For versioned builds, the source file is located at:

```text
<commit-prefix>\resources\app\product.json
```

The wildcard entry in `build/win32/code.iss` excludes only:

```text
\resources\app\product.json
```

Therefore the versioned generic file is included by the wildcard. The setup-generated target-specific file is installed by a separate explicit entry later in the `[Files]` section.

This also explains why the update cache contains `undefined`: `Win32UpdateService.cachePath` interpolates `productService.target`, while feed selection treats only `target === 'user'` as a user setup.

Related: #279149, #111107, #120515, #304999

title: Scroll-to-bottom button positioned far right in Agents view after PR #326961
description:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version:
- VS Code Version:
- OS Version:
- Feature: Agents window / scroll-to-bottom button placement
- Selected model:
- Logs: See related PR https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/326961 — exposing the existing scroll-to-bottom button in the full-width Agents transcript also exposed its shared viewport-edge positioning.

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Use a build that includes changes from PR #326961 (or recent main containing that merge).
2. Open a session in the Agents window with enough chat content to scroll.
3. Scroll away from the bottom so the scroll-to-bottom button appears.

Expected behavior:
- The scroll-to-bottom button should align with the trailing edge of the centered transcript and composer column.

Actual behavior:
- The button is rendered at the far-right edge of the full-width transcript viewport, disconnected from the centered chat content.

Notes:
- The Editor window is unaffected because its chat viewport is already width-constrained.
- The Agents window intentionally keeps the transcript viewport full width so its scrollbar stays at the window edge; only the inner transcript and composer are centered.

[View original Slack conversation](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C09MVCZKLP4/p1784939625552479?thread_ts=1784939625.552479&cid=C09MVCZKLP4)

title: Opus 5 chat loops on "thinking/redacted_thinking blocks cannot be modified" (400) in VS Code 1.130.0
description:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.58.0 (bundled)
- VS Code Version: 1.130.0 (build 1b6a188127, x64)
- OS Version: Windows
- Feature: agent mode (panel/editAgent)
- Selected model: Claude Opus 5
- Logs: added in a comment below

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Open Copilot Chat in agent mode with the Opus 5 model.
2. Continue a multi-turn conversation that includes reasoning ("thinking") blocks.
3. A turn fails with HTTP 400 "thinking or redacted_thinking blocks in the latest assistant message cannot be modified".
4. Click "Try Again".

## Summary
Apparent regression of #317097 (fixed in 1.123.0). The same 400 recurs on VS Code 1.130.0 with Claude Opus 5. Once it occurs the session is stuck: every "Try Again" resubmits the same turn and fails again with a new request id. Only switching models or starting a new chat recovers.

## Expected
Retry resends the prior thinking/redacted_thinking blocks unmodified and the conversation continues.

## Actual
Retry fails again with the identical error and a new request id, in an endless loop. Reproduces only with Opus 5; other models in the same workspace work fine.

title: Workspace-less quick chats are grouped under a raw session UUID instead of "Chats"
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- 💡 Instead of creating your report here, use 'Report Issue' from the 'Help' menu in VS Code to pre-fill useful information. -->
<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.132.0 (from sources)
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2

Steps to Reproduce:

1. In the Agents window, run an automation that creates a workspace-less session (for example a scheduled "Daily PR changelog" workflow). Alternatively, create a normal quick chat and reload the window.
2. Look at the sessions sidebar.

**Expected:** the session is grouped under the always-visible "Chats" section.

**Actual:** "Chats" reads "No chats", and the session appears under a section header labelled with its raw session UUID. The session also exposes the host's scratch directory (`~/.copilot/chats/<sessionId>`) as its workspace, which knocks on to list badges, the changes/files views, and the archive-on-delete fallback.

Once mis-grouped it stays that way across restarts, because the misclassification is also written into the sessions startup cache.

### Scope

This is not automation-specific. Whether a quick chat is affected depends on how the window first learned about it:

| Scenario | Affected |
|---|---|
| Any quick chat after a window reload | Yes |
| Quick chat created in another window or process (automations) | Yes |
| Session hydrated from the persisted startup cache | Yes |
| Quick chat created in the same, still-open window | No |

Automations just happen to be the only quick chats you never see via the local creation path, which makes the bug look automation-specific.

### Root cause

Quick-chat-ness cannot be derived from the working directory, since the host assigns workspace-less sessions a throwaway scratch cwd. It travels as an `agentHost.workspaceless` marker on the generic `_meta` bag. `AgentService.listSessions()` overlays it correctly from the per-session DB, but the AHP `root/listSessions` round-trip dropped `_meta` on both ends: `protocolServerHandler` and `RemoteAgentHostProtocolClient` each rebuild the wire item field-by-field, and `satisfies SessionSummary` does not catch a dropped optional field.

`notify/sessionAdded` does carry `_meta`, which is why a freshly created quick chat looks right in its own window. But the session adapter's kind was frozen at construction, so a session first materialized from a listing was permanently classified as workspace-backed.

Fix in progress in #327629. Follow-up for compile-time exhaustiveness guards on the mappers is tracked in #327626.

title: NES: screen reader announcement for next edit suggestions is empty (or a bare ", Inspect this in the accessible view")
description:
Found while doing a hands-on accessibility pass over Next Edit Suggestions.

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No — NES requires the GitHub Copilot extension to provide the inline edit.

- VS Code Version: 1.132.0 (built from source, `3ddd267c500`)
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.60.0
- OS Version: macOS 26.5.2

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a TypeScript file with a class that has several references to a constructor parameter.
2. Rename the parameter so the other references go stale, so NES offers a next edit suggestion.
3. Inspect the ARIA live region while the suggestion is showing:
   ```js
   document.querySelector('.monaco-aria-container').outerHTML
   ```

## Actual

The `role="alert"` region contains exactly:

```
, Inspect this in the accessible view (Option+F2)
```

Two problems:

1. **Leading comma / no content.** The message never states that a next edit suggestion is available, or where it is. "Inspect **this**" has no antecedent.
2. **With verbosity off there is no announcement at all.** When `accessibility.verbosity.inlineCompletions` is `false`, `hint` is `undefined`, so the call becomes `alert('')`, which sets `textContent = ''` and announces nothing. The only remaining cue is the audio signal.

## Cause

`src/vs/editor/contrib/inlineCompletions/browser/controller/inlineCompletionsController.ts`

```ts
if (this.editor.getOption(EditorOption.screenReaderAnnounceInlineSuggestion)) {
    if (state.kind === 'ghostText') {
        this._provideScreenReaderUpdate(state.primaryGhostText.renderForScreenReader(lineText));
    } else {
        this._provideScreenReaderUpdate(''); // Only announce Alt+F2
    }
}
```

Empty `content` is passed for the inline-edit (NES) case, and `_provideScreenReaderUpdate` then does `alert(hint ? content + ', ' + hint : content)`.

Ghost-text completions get a real spoken description; NES gets nothing.

## Expected

NES should announce something meaningful, e.g. "Next edit suggestion available on line 9, press Tab to jump" — and the accessible-view hint should be appended to that rather than being the entire message.

Related: pressing <kbd>Tab</kbd> to jump moves the cursor to a different line, which is a significant context change that also isn't announced.

### Description

In the Agents window, an attachment (image, file, selection) added to a message that is sent **while a Copilot agent is already busy** is silently dropped and never reaches the model. The message text arrives, the attachment chip renders in the UI, and nothing is logged as an error -- the agent simply behaves as if no attachment was provided (e.g. "I don't see an image").

This only affects the **steering** path (send while the agent is mid-turn) on the **Copilot** provider. It looks intermittent to users because whether an attachment survives depends purely on whether the agent happened to be busy at the moment they pressed send.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open the Agents window and start a **Copilot** agent session.
2. Send a prompt that takes a while (so the agent is mid-turn).
3. **While it is still running**, attach an image and send a message such as "what is in this image?".
4. The message is delivered as a steering message and the agent responds to the text.

**Expected:** the agent receives the attachment and can describe the image.
**Actual:** the attachment is not in the model payload; the agent says it received no image.

Sending the exact same message when the agent is **idle** works correctly.

### Root Cause

`CopilotAgentSession.sendSteering` forwards only the text and never passes the attachments to the SDK:

`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts`

```ts
async sendSteering(steeringMessage: PendingMessage): Promise<void> {
    ...
    await this._wrapper.session.send({
        prompt: steeringMessage.message.text,
        mode: 'immediate',
    });
```

`steeringMessage.message.attachments` is simply not read. The normal (idle) path in the same file does it correctly -- it maps attachments via `_toSdkAttachment` and passes them to `session.send({ prompt, attachments })`.

Everything upstream of this call does its job, which is what makes the drop so quiet:

- `AgentService._rewriteUserMessageAttachments` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts`) runs for `ChatPendingMessageSetAction` as well as `ChatTurnStartedAction`, so a steering message's attachments are already materialized to local files on the agent host side (`_rewriteSingleAttachment` -> `_readClientResource` -> `_writeAndRewrite`) before the provider is called.
- `PendingMessage.message` is a full `Message` and does carry `attachments` at this point.
- `CopilotAgent.setPendingMessages` routes only the steering message through `sendSteering`; **queued** messages are dispatched by the server through the normal `sendMessage` path, so queued messages keep their attachments and steering messages do not.

The other providers already handle this correctly, which confirms Copilot is the outlier:

- Claude -- `ClaudeAgentSession.injectSteering` (`node/claude/claudeAgentSession.ts`) passes `steeringMessage.message.attachments` to `resolvePromptToContentBlocks`.
- Codex -- `codexAgent.ts` calls `resolveCodexInput(text, steeringMessage.message.attachments)`.

### Proposed Fix

Mirror the normal send path in `sendSteering`: map `steeringMessage.message.attachments` through `_toSdkAttachment` and pass the result as `attachments` alongside `mode: 'immediate'`. This is a Copilot-only change of roughly five lines, plus a regression test in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` asserting that a steering message with attachments reaches `session.send` with those attachments.

### Notes

Found by code inspection while investigating attachment loss; a debug-log bundle reviewed at the time contained no perception failure (all image turns there were perceived, and its single steering message was text-only), so this is code-proven rather than reproduced from those logs. Unlike #327329 / #327057, this is not a preview or hydration problem -- no reload is involved, and the UI renders the attachment correctly the whole time.

title: Agents window Markdown editor: Undo and redo do not apply edits
description:
<!-- Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template -->

Testing #326540

Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes

- VS Code Version: Insiders with the experimental Markdown editor
- OS Version: macOS
- Audited package revision: microsoft/vscode-packages@1d81418d61ad769f154579196a51a9364c105e2d

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Open a Markdown document in the Agents window Markdown editor.
2. Ensure the editor is in **Editing** mode.
3. Put the caret at the end of `abc` and type `d`.
4. Press Cmd+Z.
5. Press Cmd+Shift+Z.

### Expected

Cmd+Z restores `abc`, and Cmd+Shift+Z reapplies `abcd`.

### Actual

The document remains `abcd` after both commands.

### Impact

Undo and redo are core editing safety mechanisms. Without them, users cannot recover from accidental edits and cannot trust normal VS Code editing workflows. This creates a meaningful risk of losing content, especially when editing agent-generated documents.

title: Model keeps switching back to 5.6 Sol
description:
1. Have a chat in model A
2. Interact with another chat in model B
3. Go back to the first chat, and you're now on 5.6 Sol (for me)

Marking 'important' since this will be bad for UBB users as model switches bust prompt caches.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9f489172-79cf-4cba-9c62-c81c109ae5ca

> I know there has been some work in this area, but the way I had this set up in the agent host world is that the model is retained on the draft state of the agent host session and then the model picker (and general input state) is driven off that for AH sessions--the agent host is the broker for the point of truth when seeding input for an existing chat. New chat is up to the UI to do whatever it wants. Lmk if assistance is needed here!

title: Creating a profile from the built-in Python template fails silently
label: bug
clean_text: Creating a profile from the built in Python template fails silently Type: Bug Creating a profile from the built in Python template fails silently. The profile is never created, and no error is surfaced to the user. This is the same symptom reported in 301645, which was closed as completed on 2026 03 22 ( insiders released ). The CDN hosted template still ships the entries that trigger it, and the underlying code path is still not resilient, so the failure is reproducible on current Insiders. That issue is locked, hence this new report. Steps to Reproduce 1. Run Profiles: Create Profile 2. Pick the built in Python template 3. Wait Expected The profile is created. Finished installing extensions. is never logged on any of the five attempts. Each attempt leaves a profile directory behind under User/profiles/ that is not registered in storage.json until cleanUp() prunes it on a later start. Analysis The template at returns HTTP 200 with valid JSON and lists 22 extensions, among them github.copilot and github.copilot chat . In extensionsResource.ts , ExtensionsResource.apply() installs extensions sequentially with no error handling: ts await this.extensionManagementService.requestPublisherTrust(installExtensionInfos); for (const installExtensionInfo of installExtensionInfos) { if (token.isCancellationRequested) { return; } progress?.(localize('installingExtension', "Installing extension {0}...", ...)); await this.extensionManagementService.installFromGallery(installExtensionInfo.extension, installExtensionInfo.options); } If any single installFromGallery call rejects, the whole apply() rejects, so the Finished installing extensions. line below the loop is never reached. title: Workspace skill descriptions can alter customization-index structure and suppress external-file confirmation
description:
<!-- MSRC assessed this behavior as low severity and recommended filing a public product-hardening issue. This report intentionally omits weaponized payloads and sensitive data. -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: `0.59.0`
- VS Code Version: latest `main`, commit `dd862885ff5fbd279747c793e18105e6b7ddc805`
- OS Version: Windows 11 `10.0.26200` build `26200`
- Feature: Agent mode, workspace skills, ReadFile tool
- Selected model: No live model is required for the deterministic test
- Logs: Local unit-test output only; no production service was contacted

## Summary

A workspace skill description is inserted into the XML-like chat customizations index without structural escaping. The generated text is later parsed back into instruction and skill file sets used by the external-file ReadFile confirmation logic.

As a result, delimiter characters in workspace-controlled skill metadata can alter the generated index structure and cause an outside-workspace URI to be classified as an instruction file. ReadFile then omits the confirmation that the safe control receives.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Check out commit `dd862885ff5fbd279747c793e18105e6b7ddc805`.
2. Create a workspace `SKILL.md` whose valid frontmatter description contains XML delimiter characters that terminate the generated description element and introduce a synthetic instruction/file record.
3. Build the customizations index through `AutomaticInstructionsCollector`.
4. Parse the generated index through `CustomInstructionsService.parseInstructionIndexFile`.
5. Prepare a ReadFile invocation for the synthetic outside-workspace URI.
6. Compare it with an otherwise identical control using a normal skill description.

Local deterministic test result on latest `main`:

```text
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       1 passed (1)
```

The control produced confirmation messages. The structurally altered index did not.

## Expected Behavior

Workspace-controlled skill names, descriptions, and paths should be encoded as data and must not be able to add records to the generated customization index or influence external-file authorization.

## Actual Behavior

The skill description is interpolated as markup. The later index parser accepts the additional structure, and the resulting URI is treated as an external instruction file for which ReadFile confirmation is not shown.

## Relevant Source

- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/promptFiles/node/automaticInstructionsCollector.ts:497-504` constructs the skill entry and interpolates `skill.description`.
- `extensions/copilot/src/platform/customInstructions/common/customInstructionsService.ts:501-585` parses the model-facing text back into instruction and skill URI sets.
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/toolUtils.ts:217-233` exempts URIs present in those parsed sets from the normal outside-workspace rejection.
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/tools/node/readFileTool.tsx:207-244` prepares the ReadFile confirmation.

## Impact and Scope

This is a confirmation/security-boundary consistency issue. It can cause a file outside the workspace to be returned to the configured model without the expected external-file confirmation.

The reproduced behavior requires the outer Copilot/workspace-trust requirements and an agent ReadFile request for the affected path. The test does not demonstrate command execution or direct exfiltration to a workspace-controlled server.

## Suggested Fix

- Escape every dynamic field before including it in the model-facing XML-like representation.
- Prefer a structured, non-text authorization object rather than reparsing prompt text.
- Do not derive external-file authorization from a representation containing workspace-controlled display metadata.
- Add a regression test with delimiter characters in skill metadata and assert that the safe and adversarial cases both require confirmation for the same outside-workspace URI.

## Existing-Issue Review

I searched issues and pull requests in `microsoft/vscode` and `microsoft/vscode-copilot-release` using the relevant class names, parser names, external-file confirmation terminology, and skill-description wording.

Adjacent issues `#292297`, `#295643`, and `#305168` concern legitimate skill files incorrectly receiving confirmation or being inaccessible. They do not describe workspace metadata altering the customization-index structure or suppressing confirmation. Issue `#301966` concerns losing the index during context compaction.

title: Agent Host session returns to plan mode after plan approval and reload
description:
## Steps to reproduce

1. Start an Agent Host session in Plan mode.
2. Let the agent create a plan.
3. Accept the plan and choose an implementation mode such as Interactive.
4. Let the agent finish, then reload or reopen the session later.

## Expected

The session remains in the mode selected when the plan was accepted.

## Actual

The session returns to Plan mode after it is restored.

## Root cause

Plan acceptance correctly updates the live AHP session config through a server-dispatched `session/configChanged` action. However, merged session config values are persisted only from the client-action side-effect path. Server-originated mode changes therefore update the picker and live state but leave the persisted `configValues.mode` as `plan`, which is restored on reload.

Session-config persistence should observe applied action envelopes regardless of whether the action originated from a client or the server.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Agents window can select a hidden agent on the new chat page
description:
Found while running the experiment that replaces the extension-host Copilot CLI with the Agent Host Copilot CLI.

The Agents window can end up with the **extension-host Copilot CLI agent selected on the new chat page even though that agent is hidden from the harness picker**. You should never be able to have an agent selected that isn't actually offered in the picker — if it's hidden, it must not be selectable, and sending from that state targets an agent the user can't see or choose.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Set these settings:

   ```jsonc
   "chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost": true,
   "chat.agentHost.enabled": true,
   "chat.agentHost.defaultSessionsProvider": true,
   ```

2. Open the Agents window. The harness picker on the new chat page correctly offers only the Agent Host Copilot entry — the extension-host Copilot CLI is hidden.
3. From the sessions list, open an **existing extension-host Copilot CLI session** (one created before the setting was turned on).
4. Press the **New** button (or <kbd>Cmd+N</kbd>) to go back to the new chat page.

**Expected:** the new chat page shows an agent that the harness picker actually offers (the Agent Host Copilot).

**Actual:** the extension-host Copilot CLI is shown as the selected agent, even though it is absent from the picker dropdown. The workspace folder is also silently dropped.

## Notes on the cause

Two "remember the previously selected agent" mechanisms compound:

1. `NewChatInSessionsWindowAction` passes the active session's `providerId` + `sessionType` straight to `openNewSession`. Since the extension-host Copilot CLI is no longer advertised, `_resolveProviderForNewSession` throws `does not advertise session type 'copilotcli'`, and `openNewSession` swallows the error with only a trace log — so no session is created on either provider and the composer lands with no active session.
2. With no session, `SessionTypePicker._computeCurrentPick()` falls back to the stored `sessions.userSelectedSessionType` pick without validating it against the session types the dropdown actually renders.

The same unguarded inheritance exists in the archived-session fallback in `SessionsService`.

(Written by Copilot)

title: Agent Host model catalogs are not refreshed periodically
description:
## Problem

Agent Host model catalogs are loaded only on provider-specific edge triggers such as authentication, transport changes, or process startup. A long-lived Agent Host therefore does not discover a model added by the backing service until the token rotates or the host restarts.

Copilot model enumeration also has no long-term retry after its bounded startup retries are exhausted, and a Copilot CLI client restart can continue exposing a catalog loaded by the previous client or endpoint.

## Expected behavior

Each registered Agent Host provider should refresh its available model catalog every 10 minutes from a single host-owned scheduler. Transient refresh failures should preserve the last known-good catalog, while intentional provider source changes should invalidate stale entries.

## Related pull request

Implemented by [#327408](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327408).

(Written by Copilot)

title: Agent host session hangs forever when a startup-config change restarts the CLI client mid-turn
description:
Agent host: a startup-config change (`sessionSync`) restarts the CLI client mid-turn and the session hangs forever

## What happens

`CopilotAgent._restartClientIfStartupConfigChanged()` tears down the CopilotClient whenever a startup-only config value changes, **even if a turn is actively running**:

```ts
if (this._client) {
    this._logService.info(`[Copilot] Startup config changed (${changed}), restarting CopilotClient`);
    this._sessions.clearAndDisposeAll();
    await this._stopClient();
}
```

`CopilotAgentSession` never finalizes its in-flight turn on disposal — `ChatTurnComplete` / `ChatTurnCancelled` / `ChatError` are only emitted in response to SDK events (`_completeActiveTurn`, `_beginSteeringTurn`). A disposed session gets no more SDK events, so nothing closes the turn.

Net effect: the client's turn stays open forever. The UI spins with no output, no error, and no way to recover other than reloading.

## Evidence (from an Agent Host debug log bundle)

| Time (local) | Event |
|---|---|
| 09:05:03 | `chat/turnStarted turnId=request_bbf818da-…` |
| 09:05–09:26 | ~30 tool calls run normally under that turn |
| 09:26:44 | `Tool started: apply_patch`, `assistant.turn_start` — model still working |
| 09:27:02 | `[DefaultAccount] Managed settings fetch returned non-success status 404; falling back to local-only policy` |
| **09:27:06** | **`[Copilot] Startup config changed (sessionSync=true), restarting CopilotClient`** |
| 09:27:07 | `session.shutdown`; CLI subprocess exits |
| after | **No `chat/turnComplete`, no `chat/turnCancelled`, no `chat/error`** is ever sent for `request_bbf818da` |
| 11:36 | ~2h later the user exports logs; session still shows as running |

The agent host process itself stayed healthy — it kept serving a different session for another 2 hours. Only the session with the in-flight turn was orphaned.

Note that `sessionSync` maps to `chat.sessionSync.enabled`, which is experiment-driven (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`) and policy-controlled (`CopilotSessionSync` / `cloud_session_storage_enabled`). It can flip on its own from an async experiment or policy refresh, so this can kill a running turn with **no user action at all**. That's what happened here — the flip landed 4s after a managed-settings fetch 404'd.

## How it regressed

The original implementation only restarted when idle — https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/317390 (`5d8b31703319`):

```ts
if (this._client && this._sessions.size === 0) {
    ...
    await this._stopClient();
}
```

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/319430 (`225f0854cc65`) removed the `_sessions.size === 0` guard so the rubber duck toggle would take effect immediately. That PR's own commit message notes the change: *"Corrects the misleading 'only if idle' restart comment to match the new behavior (active sessions are disposed on a startup-config change)."*

Later PRs added more restart triggers to the same unguarded path (`enterpriseHost`, `copilotSdkLogLevel`, `systemProxy`), widening the window.

## Suggested fix

Two independent problems, both worth fixing:

1. **Don't kill live work.** Restore an idle check: defer the restart until all sessions are idle (or at minimum until no turn is running), rather than disposing sessions mid-turn. Especially important because `sessionSync` can change without any user action.
2. **Never leave a turn open.** Finalize the in-flight turn when a `CopilotAgentSession` is disposed — emit `ChatError` (or `ChatTurnCancelled`) + `ChatTurnComplete` so the client stops spinning and the user sees something actionable. This should be dispose-driven so it also covers `shutdown()` and `releaseSession()`.

## Possibly related

At 16:06:46Z a steering turn was started and completed while the original turn was still open, with no `turnComplete` for the original — so the chat had two overlapping open turns even before the restart. May be a separate `_beginSteeringTurn` bug.

*(Written by Copilot)*

title: Voice mode: improve listening-state contrast across themes
description:
## Problem

The existing listening indication can be too low-contrast in some themes, leaving users unsure whether voice mode is actively listening.

## Desired behavior

- The active listening rim and icon should remain visually distinct from the chat input background.
- Theme customizations should be respected.
- High-contrast theme behavior must remain intact.
- Reduced-motion behavior must remain intact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Resolve the active rim against the actual `inputBackground` theme color.
- [x] Maintain at least 3:1 non-text contrast for the active indication.
- [x] Cover representative light and dark custom input backgrounds with unit tests.
- [x] Verify the simulated listening state in an isolated workbench launch.

Implemented by #329493.

title: Voice Mode ambient glow redesign: verify it applies uniformly across the normal and Agents windows
description:
Tracking issue for the Voice Mode ambient glow redesign.

| PR | Scope | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328455 | The rim redesign across the chat inputs | Merged |
| https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328484 | Dictation mic glow uniformity | In review |

Voice Mode's ambient glow is currently a hardcoded blue/purple border plus box-shadow, applied identically on every surface. It reads as a focus ring rather than as a microphone being open, and it can't follow the theme.

The redesign replaces it with a single ambient light that says **who currently holds the floor**:

| State | Treatment |
| --- | --- |
| `listening` | Audio-reactive interior rim, cool |
| `speaking` | The same rim, shifted warm |
| everything else | Nothing |

Colors derive from the theme accent (`chat.voiceGlowBaseColor`, defaulting to `focusBorder`) instead of being hardcoded, and high contrast themes opt out of the soft rim in favour of a solid line.

## Why this needs tracking

This is a UX change that touches every voice surface across two windows, so it needs verifying that it (a) doesn't regress anything around the chat input and (b) **applies uniformly** — the same glow, the same colors, the same states, everywhere voice appears.

## Surfaces in scope

| Window | Surface | Wiring |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Normal window | Chat view (panel / sidebar / editor) | `chatViewPane.ts` |
| Agents window | Agent session chat view | `chatView.ts` |
| Agents window | Agent welcome / new chat view | `newChatVoice.ts` |
| Agents window | Agents voice widget | `agentsVoiceWidget.ts` |

## Verification

### Uniformity — the same treatment on every surface

For each of the four surfaces above:

- [ ] `listening` shows the cool rim; `speaking` shows the warm rim
- [ ] No glow in any other state (idle, processing, error, disconnected)
- [ ] `listening -> speaking` cross-fades rather than snapping
- [ ] The rim follows the input's corner radius on all four corners
- [ ] The mic glyph, voice pill and waveform all read the same accent as the rim

### No regressions around the chat input

- [ ] Send button is visible and clickable while the glow is active (it sits above the glow at `z-index: 12`)
- [ ] The full input toolbar stays available during voice — attachments, model picker, mode picker, settings
- [ ] The transcript overlay still renders correctly under the glow
- [ ] The glow is removed cleanly when voice stops, with no stale frame left behind
- [ ] No layout shift when the glow appears or disappears

### Theming

- [ ] Dark, light and high contrast (high contrast should show a solid line, not a soft rim)
- [ ] Glow follows a custom `chat.voiceGlowBaseColor`
- [ ] `chat.voiceListeningGlow` / `chat.voiceSpeakingGlow` pin individual states

### Accessibility and performance

- [ ] `workbench.reduceMotion: on` pins a still frame and swaps layers without cross-fading
- [ ] The OS-level reduced motion setting is honoured
- [ ] The animation frame loop only runs while a glow is actually rendered
- [ ] No new focusable or screen-reader-announced content (the glow is decorative)

## Dictation

Dictation originally picked up the shared accent token but painted it raw, while the rim paints a tuned version (hue nudged, saturation bounded, lightness pinned per theme) — so an open microphone looked different depending on which feature opened it.

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/328484 fixes both halves: it moves that tuning into one shared helper both features resolve through, and mounts the actual rim on the microphone (scaled to the button) so it breathes like the chat input instead of pulsing.

- [ ] Dictation mic wears the actual rim (uneven, breathing light), not a uniform pulse
- [ ] Dictation mic glow matches the Voice Mode listening rim color, in light and dark
- [ ] Rim scales sensibly to the button and doesn't break into arcs or swamp the glyph
- [ ] Verified on all three dictation mics: chat execute toolbar, segmented voice-input pill, Agents window composer
- [ ] A theme pinning `chat.dictationActiveMicGlow` still wins, and is tuned the same way
- [ ] High contrast shows the same solid blue line as the listening rim

/cc @meganrogge

title: Dictation: Add a multilingual Nemotron model with language settings for the model
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

First of all, thank you for adding this feature to VS Code; now a proper ASR model is used instead of the poor transcription from the VS Code Speech plugin.

However, as shipped in 1.131 it is designed only for English-speaking users. This is a regression: in 1.130 the multilingual model was the **default**. From the test plan (#326388):

> Nemotron **(default)** - `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`. Multilingual (35+ languages, auto-detected). [...] Verify it transcribes in that language without any language setting.

In 1.131 the default became `nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b`, and the `dictation.model` enum only offers that one plus `mai`, so the multilingual model can no longer be selected. There is also a migration that rewrites the multilingual id back to the English one, so users who had it configured lose it.

I see that in your `foundry.modelinfo.json` it is already available as `nemotron-3.5-asr-streaming-0.6b`, so it can just be used again.

You also need to add the language the model will work with. Only switching the model is not enough: if I set `dictation.model` to the multilingual one by hand it does work, but without an explicit language it runs in auto-detect mode and on short phrases it keeps guessing English and transliterates instead (`privet` instead of `привет`).

You can get the list of languages for the config from here:
https://docs.nvidia.com/nim/speech/latest/reference/support-matrix/asr.html#asr-nemotron-asr-streaming-supported-languages

You can set the parameter as `"dictation.speechLanguage": "ru-RU"` in settings.json. Or maybe reuse the existing `accessibility.voice.speechLanguage`, so there are not two settings for the same thing.

### Version

VS Code 1.131.0 (`e4c7e7b1d6d060162f4aa7f8225271b67ce1df75`), Windows 11

title: Inline terminal preview wraps output at fixed width instead of chat panel width
description:
The inline terminal output preview in chat wraps content at a fixed column count (80 for restored sessions, or whatever the backing panel terminal happens to be for live ones) instead of the actual width of the output box. On a wide chat panel long lines wrap way too early and there is a dead gap before the chevron. Resizing the panel doesn't re-wrap the content either.

The detached xterm mirror gets its cols once at creation in chatTerminalCommandMirror.ts and we never resize it after that.

Way to verify:
Run something like `python3 -c "print('The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog. ' * 20)"` in agent mode and expand the output preview. The wrap point should match the box width, and dragging the sidebar wider/narrower should re-wrap the content live.

title: Provide an easier way to use dictation in disconnected environments
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->

I was trying out the new dictation feature and ran into an issue where my corporate firewall blocks access to the catalog/model registry (api.catalog.azureml.ms) so the initial retrieval of nemotron fails.

Digging through the VS Code source, Foundry Local SDK, and some docs I fortunately found links to download the models documented in [DISCONNECTED_CATALOG.md](https://github.com/Azure-Samples/foundry-local-model-catalog/blob/main/DISCONNECTED_CATALOG.md#foundry-extension-expansion-packs) and could sideload the model and get things working by dropping things into their appropriate places on the filesystem.

We often run VS Code in environments that have restricted or no connectivity. For whatever it is worth, I had Claude write up some notes of my journey to get it working and have attached it as [vscode-dictation-sideload-github.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30530346/vscode-dictation-sideload-github.md).

Is there a world where this workflow could be better supported/documented? Maybe CC to @meganrogge?

Thank you

title: Agent Host terminal auto-approve should use PowerShell grammar for PowerShell commands
description:
Follow up to #326766 and #324136. PR #327947 adds persistent user/workspace auto-approve actions to Agent Host Copilot terminal confirmations, but there is still a parser mismatch for the SDK's `powershell` tool.

The workbench generates suggestions using the PowerShell tree-sitter grammar, while Agent Host's `commandAutoApprover.ts` only loads `tree-sitter-bash.wasm` for eligibility and enforcement.

Impact:

- **Existing settings rule:** a simple rule such as `"Get-ChildItem": true` usually works because bash can treat it as a generic command name. Rules for PowerShell-specific syntax can still miss because Agent Host splits/interprets the command using bash grammar.
- **Rule added from #327947:** the workbench can suggest and persist a rule from an accurate PowerShell parse, but Agent Host re-parses the next command as bash. The user selects "Always Allow" and is prompted again.
- **Exact command-line rule:** this can also miss when bash parsing fails because Agent Host parses before checking the exact command-line allow rule.

Representative cases include pipelines with script blocks (`Where-Object { ... }`), `$()` subexpressions, backtick continuations, PowerShell operators, and PowerShell-specific redirects such as `$null`.

The expected failure mode is conservative re-prompting/inconsistent suggestions; Agent Host remains authoritative for approval. There is no known auto-approval bypass from this mismatch.

Work needed:

- Load `tree-sitter-powershell.wasm` in the Agent Host command auto-approver (it already ships in the same package).
- Carry/select the shell grammar for both rule eligibility and enforcement.
- Add coverage for existing settings rules and rules created from #327947, including PowerShell-specific sub-command and exact-command-line cases.

Related forwarding work: #322774.

title: Mouse back/forward buttons do not navigate in the Agents window
description:
The mouse back/forward buttons (buttons 4/5) navigate editor history in the main VS Code window, but do nothing in the Agents window.

This is inconsistent with the keyboard, where `Alt+Left` / `Alt+Right` already navigate between sessions in the Agents window.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Agents window.
2. Visit two or more sessions so there is session history.
3. Press the mouse back button.

**Expected:** navigate to the previously visited session, matching `Alt+Left`.
**Actual:** nothing happens.

### Cause

The shared mouse handler in `HistoryService.onMouseDownOrUp` calls `goBack()` / `goForward()` on the **editor** history service directly, bypassing command and keybinding resolution. Since no `when`-clause routing applies, the mouse never reaches the Agents window's session history (`SessionsNavigation`, exposed through `ISessionsService.openPreviousSession()` / `openNextSession()`), and the editor history it falls through to is usually empty in that window.

This is why the keyboard path works (it is routed by `when` clauses on `EditorAreaFocusContext`) while the mouse path does not.

### Notes

Both histories are intentionally live in the Agents window: editor history still applies to the docked side pane (Changes multi-diff, Files, file diffs). So the fix needs to route by focus rather than replace one with the other.

A possible broader follow-up is to have the `HistoryService` mouse handler dispatch `workbench.action.navigateBack` / `navigateForward` through `ICommandService` so `when` clauses decide the target, which would give any window contributing higher-weight bindings for those chords mouse support automatically.

Fixed by #327432.

title: Use ARIA status instead of alert for terminal live updates
description:
## Type of issue

Feature request

## Current behavior

Terminal live updates are announced through an ARIA alert. Frequent terminal output makes these assertive announcements noisy and disruptive for screen reader users.

## Proposed behavior

Use an ARIA status announcement for terminal live updates so updates remain available to screen readers without interrupting other speech.

title: Allow terminal accessible view to always preserve cursor position
description:
## Type of issue

Feature request

## Current behavior

`terminal.integrated.accessibleViewPreserveCursorPosition` preserves the cursor position until new command output arrives, then moves the accessible view to the bottom.

## Proposed behavior

Change the setting from a boolean to an enum while preserving the current behavior as the default. Add an option that always preserves the cursor position, including when new command output arrives.

Existing boolean values should continue to map to equivalent behavior for compatibility.

title: Voice: respect disabled hands-free mode when starting and stopping listening
description:
### Problem

When `agents.voice.handsFree` is disabled, pressing the voice mode button automatically activates listening. Stopping listening then automatically sends the transcribed input.

This makes the non-hands-free experience behave like hands-free mode and prevents users from controlling listening and submission separately.

### Expected behavior

When hands-free mode is disabled:

- Pressing the voice mode button should enter voice mode without automatically activating listening.
- Stopping listening should stop transcription without automatically sending the input.
- Sending should remain an explicit user action.

Follow-up to #327217.

title: Incrementally refine dictation while recording
description:
Depends on #327211.

The language-model cleanup added by #327211 runs only after dictation stops. For longer dictation sessions, we could improve responsiveness and reduce the final cleanup latency by periodically refining only the trailing portion of the transcript while the user is still speaking.

## Proposal

- Periodically reprocess only the trailing **N seconds** of dictation, or the **last sentence**, rather than sending the full transcript on every update.
- Keep the earlier, already-refined prefix stable so text does not churn while the user dictates.
- On each refinement, replace only the matching trailing segment with the cleaned result.
- Preserve the existing final cleanup pass when dictation stops, including its cancellation, timeout, length-limit, and raw-transcript fallback behavior.
- Avoid overlapping refinement requests; a newer trailing segment should supersede stale work.

## Goals

- Show punctuation, casing, and filler-word cleanup during dictation.
- Reduce perceived latency when dictation ends.
- Bound model input and request frequency for long sessions.
- Prevent partial or stale model responses from corrupting the transcript.

## Open questions

- Whether the refinement boundary should be time-based, sentence-based, or a combination of both.
- What interval and trailing-window size provide the best quality/latency tradeoff.
- Whether incremental cleanup should remain behind `dictation.experimental.llmCleanup` or have a separate experimental setting.

title: Voice: do not auto-send the turn by default when hands-free mode is disabled
description:
### Problem

In voice mode, the turn is auto-sent (ended) on trailing silence (`agents.voice.turn.silenceMs`, default `800`) and on a stop phrase (`agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases`, default `['send it']`) regardless of whether hands-free mode (`agents.voice.handsFree`) is enabled.

When a user turns **off** hands-free mode, they are opting out of the automatic back-and-forth loop and expect to control when each turn is sent. Auto-ending the turn on silence in that case is surprising and can send a turn before the user is done speaking.

### Proposal

When `agents.voice.handsFree` is **disabled**, do not auto-send the turn by default:

- Suppress trailing-silence turn ending unless `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs` has been explicitly configured.
- Suppress stop-phrase turn ending unless `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases` has been explicitly configured.

Users who explicitly configure either setting keep that behavior. Update the setting descriptions for `agents.voice.turn.silenceMs` and `agents.voice.turn.stopPhrases` (and `agents.voice.handsFree`) to document this.

title: Built-in dictation should filter filler words ("um", "uh") from the transcript
description:
### Feature request

Our built-in on-device dictation transcribes speech disfluencies (filler words) literally, so dictated text is cluttered with "um", "uh", "erm", etc.:

> um so uh i was umm thinking about it

We should strip standalone filler tokens from the finalized transcript, including lengthened variants (`um`/`umm`, `uh`/`uhh`, `uhm`, `er`/`erm`, `hm`/`hmm`), while keeping real words that merely contain those letters ("huh", "duh", "summon") intact.

Expected result:

> so i was thinking about it

title: Agents Window: make custom session groups easier to discover/create
description:
Summary

Agents Window has a useful custom-groups feature for organizing sessions (implemented by Benjamin Simmonds) but it is hard to discover and use because the only way to create a custom group is to right-click an existing session. You cannot right-click the blank area or a built-in group header (e.g., project headers) to create a new group.

Problem

- Discovery: Most team members aren't aware this feature exists because there is no obvious UI affordance for creating groups.
- Interaction limitation: You can only create a custom group by right-clicking an existing session. Right-clicking the blank space or a project/header doesn't show the option.

Proposed enhancement

Please add one or more of the following to improve discoverability and usability:

- Allow right-click on blank space in Agents Window to create a new custom group.
- Allow right-clicking built-in group headers (project headers) to create or manage custom sub-groups.
- Add a visible "New group" / "+" button in the Agents Window toolbar or header to create groups without needing a session to be present.
- Add a brief tooltip or hint the first time a user opens Agents Window indicating groups can be created (or a discoverability hint in the command palette).

Rationale

These changes will make the feature discoverable to more users and remove the awkward requirement of needing an existing session to create groups. The feature is valuable (see screenshot shared by the reporter) but is currently hidden behind a non-obvious interaction.

Notes

- Reporter: sbatten (shared feedback in Slack).
- Implemented example: Benjamin Simmonds has a working custom-groups implementation in Agents Window — consider aligning the UX around easier creation flows.

Thank you!

title: Git detection: `.gitignore` handling differs between scan and open-editors
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
VS Code detects repositories two ways, and they treat a parent `.gitignore` **oppositely**:

| Mechanism | Setting | Honors `.gitignore`? | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subfolder scan | `git.repositoryScanMaxDepth` | **No** | Finds repos in ignored folders, but bulk-adds *all* of them |
| Open-editors | `autoRepositoryDetection: openEditors` | **Yes** | On-demand per opened file, but suppressed inside ignored folders |

Because they disagree, one natural behavior is unreachable: **register a repo only when I open one of its files, even if it lives in an ignored folder.** `repositoryScanMaxDepth` bulk-adds everything; `scanRepositories` is a static hand-kept list; `openEditors` is suppressed by `.gitignore`.

This matters for repos actively developed inside a dependency/output folder the outer repo ignores (package/vendor dirs, vendored sources). Un-ignoring the folder isn't viable.

**Proposal:** a single setting applied to **both** mechanisms:

```jsonc
"git.detectRepositoriesInIgnoredFolders": false // default = current behavior
```

When `true`, neither the scan nor open-editors is suppressed by a parent `.gitignore`. Folder exclusions stay controlled by the explicit `git.repositoryScanIgnoredFolders` list.

Related: #41565 — its fix covered the scan-depth path only; the on-demand/open-editors case inside ignored folders is the gap here.

title: Voice Mode: replace configuration gear buttons with mic context-menu actions
description:
