- a **keybinding gear** on the `AgentsVoiceWidget` (opens the Voice Mode keybinding editor), and

These gears add toolbar clutter, are inconsistent between the normal window and the Agents window, and don't match how the dictation mic button exposes its actions (via a right-click context menu).

### Proposal

- **Configure Keybinding** — opens the Voice Mode keybinding editor (what the keybinding gear did).
- **Voice Mode Settings** — opens the Voice Mode settings (what the settings gear did).
- plus the existing **Select Microphone** and **Disable Voice Mode** entries.

No gear button should show in either the normal window or the Agents window while Voice Mode is active.

### Tracking
Implemented by #327042.

title: Extend built-in on-device dictation to editor dictation, terminal voice, and add read-aloud (TTS)
description:
### Summary

Now that VS Code has a built-in on-device dictation engine (`ILocalTranscriptionService`, gated by `chat.speechToText.enabled` / `chatSpeechToTextConfigured`), we should extend it to cover the remaining speech surfaces that today only work through the `ms-vscode.vscode-speech` extension. Doing so lets built-in speech fully supersede the extension for dictation + read-aloud, so we can retire the "disable the redundant Speech extension" prompt entirely.

Related: we've already made the built-in chat mic win over the extension mic (single mic icon) and gated the extension's chat keybinding. The extension still uniquely provides the surfaces below.

### Scope

Extend the built-in on-device engine to power:

- [ ] **Editor dictation** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/codeEditor/browser/dictation/editorDictation.ts` (currently gated on `HasSpeechProvider`, uses the extension's `ISpeechService`). Route it through `ILocalTranscriptionService` when built-in dictation is configured.
- [ ] **Terminal voice dictation** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/voice/browser/terminalVoice.ts` / `terminalVoiceActions.ts`. Same: use the built-in engine when available.
- [ ] **Read aloud / text-to-speech** — the extension is the only provider of `ITextToSpeechSession` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/speech/common/speechService.ts`). Built-in has no TTS today. Add an on-device (or platform) TTS path so "Read Aloud" in chat works without the extension.

### Motivation

- Built-in on-device speech is private (no audio leaves the machine) and ships in the box.
- Once these three surfaces are covered, `ms-vscode.vscode-speech` becomes fully redundant for dictation and read-aloud, so the redundant-extension notification can be removed rather than asking users to disable a still-useful extension.
- Consistent UX: one speech stack, one set of keybindings, no double mic / keybinding collisions.

### Notes / open questions

- Keep the extension's keyword activation ("Hey Code") in mind — decide whether that stays extension-only or is also brought in-box.
- Gate every new surface on the same `chatSpeechToTextConfigured` predicate and fall back to the extension where built-in on-device transcription is unsupported (web/remote or `chat.speechToText.enabled: false`).
- TTS may need a separate on-device model / platform API investigation; it's the largest unknown here.

title: Refine quick-chat row rendering in the Sessions list (compact single-line rows)
description:
Implemented by #326148 and #326287: refines how the Sessions list renders rows for **quick chats** vs regular sessions in the Agents window.

- **Quick-chat rows are now single-line and compact** (#326148): smaller icon, tighter row height, and no second (details) row — no type icon, diff stats, timestamp, or "Working..." text (their spinner status icon already conveys progress).
- **Per-row chat icon suppression is now unconditional** (#326287): quick chats never show a chat/PR glyph on their status icon, regardless of section (Chats, Pinned, or a custom group). Their identity is conveyed by the section they render in. (This supersedes the earlier behavior where the chat icon showed outside the Chats section.)
- Fixed icon/title alignment for quick-chat rows, including phone layout, so the title stays aligned even when an approval/CI row grows the row taller.
- Regular sessions are unchanged: they keep the standard two-line row (type icon, diff stats, status/description, relative timestamp).

## Verification steps
1. In the Agents window, create a **quick chat** and a **regular session** with changes.
2. ✅ The quick chat renders as a **single-line, compact** row (small icon, no second details row).
3. ✅ The regular session keeps the **two-line** row (type icon, diff stats, status, timestamp).
4. Pin the quick chat or move it to a custom group → ✅ it **never** shows a chat/PR glyph on its status icon in any section.
5. Trigger an approval/CI row on a quick chat (and check phone layout) → ✅ icon and title stay aligned, no clipping/overflow against the next row.

title: Agent Host input box missing fuzzy file search (e.g. '#roadma' → roadmap.md)
description:
Summary

The agent host's input box doesn't seem to support the same fuzzy file search behavior as the Local harness. For example, in the Local harness typing `#roadma` finds `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/roadmap.md`, but using the agent host input box (regardless of harness) does not find that file.

Example / Reproduction

1. In the Local harness input box type: `#roadma`
2. It finds `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/roadmap.md`.
3. In the agent host input box type: `#roadma`
4. It does not find the file.

Expected behavior

The agent host input box should support the same fuzzy file search (including prefixing with `#`) as the Local harness so that shorthand queries like `#roadma` match `roadmap.md` and similar files.

Why this is useful

Having consistent fuzzy file search across the Local harness and agent host makes it faster to locate files when interacting with agents and reduces friction for workflows that rely on shorthand/prefix searches.

Notes

- Assigning to @roblourens — if you're not the right person please feel free to reassign to whoever owns the agent host fuzzy-search behavior.

title: Agent Host: Return an error for unsupported requests before initialize
description:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

When a client sends a JSON-RPC request other than `initialize`, `reconnect`, `ping`, or `_vscodeUpgrade` before completing the Agent Host Protocol handshake, the agent host currently stays silent. Please return a JSON-RPC error instead, preferably `MethodNotFound` (`-32601`) for an unknown method (or an explicit not-initialized error if that is a better protocol contract).

A silent response leaves generic JSON-RPC clients waiting until their own timeout and makes an incompatible protocol/handshake look like a transport failure.

### Standalone Node.js reproduction

```js
const ws = new WebSocket('ws://localhost:4123?tkn=<connection-token>');

ws.addEventListener('open', () => {
  ws.send(JSON.stringify({
    jsonrpc: '2.0',
    id: 1,
    method: 'notARealMethod',
    params: { channel: 'ahp-root://' },
  }));
});

ws.addEventListener('message', event => {
  console.log(String(event.data));
});
```

Observed against the local VS Code agent host: the WebSocket opens, but no response arrives within 3 seconds.

This was also verified after a valid AHP `initialize`: the same unknown request then receives an immediate error. The current post-initialize response uses `-32603` (JSON-RPC Internal error):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 2,
  "error": {
    "code": -32603,
    "message": "Unknown method: notARealMethod"
  }
}
```

The silent behavior is therefore specific to pre-initialize dispatch. Ideally, unknown methods should consistently return JSON-RPC `MethodNotFound` (`-32601`) rather than `InternalError` (`-32603`).

### Expected

The server responds to every JSON-RPC request with either a result or an error, including before initialization. For the request above, for example:

```json
{

title: Editor type dropdown in the breadcrumbs bar to switch/set the editor for a file
description: ### Problem When a file can be opened by more than one editor (for example a `*.md` file that can open in the text editor, the Markdown preview, or the Markdown editor), there is no obvious, always-visible way to see which editor is currently used or to switch to another one. Today users have to know about the `Reopen Editor With…` command, and there is no affordance in the editor chrome that surfaces the available editors. This is especially relevant now that custom editors opt out of diffs/merges by default (#324791): users may want to quickly switch a diff between the text diff editor and a custom diff editor, or set a per-extension default. ### Proposal Add a small dropdown on the right-hand side of the **breadcrumbs bar** that shows the current editor type as text (for example "Markdown Preview", "Text Editor", or "Text Diff Editor" in a diff) and, when clicked, opens a menu to: - **Switch** the active editor to any of the other editors that can open the resource (reuses `reopenActiveEditorWith`). The current editor is checked. - **Set Default** for the file type via a submenu. In a diff context this writes to `workbench.diffEditorAssociations`; otherwise to `workbench.editorAssociations`. The currently configured default is checked. - In a diff, **Open Original** / **Open Modified** as standalone editors. Details: - The dropdown only appears when a **more specialized editor is available** — i.e. more than one editor can open the resource. It is hidden for plain text files (only the default editor) and for exclusive editors such as the Hex editor (which return no alternatives). - Extension-provided editors show their source (`Label - Extension Name`); built-in editors show just their label. - In a diff context, the default text editor is labeled "Text Diff Editor" to match how it actually opens. - Only shown on the dedicated breadcrumbs bar (tabbed mode), not the inline single-tab breadcrumbs. - Behind an experimental setting `breadcrumbs.showEditorType` (default `true`). ### Verification steps 1. Ensure a file type has multiple editors (e.g. Markdown: text editor + Markdown preview). Open a `*.md` file. 2. The breadcrumbs bar shows a dropdown on the right with the current editor type (e.g. "Text Editor"). 3. Click it → menu lists the available editors with the current one checked; picking another reopens the file with it. 4. Use the **Set Default** submenu → the chosen editor is written to `workbench.editorAssociations` for `*.md` and becomes the default. 5. Open a `*.md` diff → the dropdown shows "Text Diff Editor"; the **Set Default (Diff Only)** submenu writes to `workbench.diffEditorAssociations`; **Open Original** / **Open Modified** open each side. 6. Open a plain `*.txt` file (only the default editor) or a file handled by an exclusive editor (Hex) → the dropdown is hidden. 7. Set `"breadcrumbs.showEditorType": false` → the dropdown disappears; set it back to `true` → it returns.

title: Add never editor priority so custom editors opt out of diff/merge by default
description:
### Problem

When an extension registers a custom editor with `default` priority for a file type, that editor also hijacks the **diff** and **merge** views for that file type. This happens purely from the contribution — no `workbench.editorAssociations` entry is needed — because diff/merge inherit the `textEditor` priority. So an extension has no way to provide a great normal editor for a file type without also taking over its diffs and merges.

The same applies when a user opts a custom editor in via settings. For example:

```jsonc
"workbench.editorAssociations": {
  "*.md": "vscode.markdown.editor"
}
```

...makes `*.md` diffs open the Markdown editor side-by-side instead of the normal text diff editor. The only escape hatch is an **opt-out** per extension: users have to add a second setting to reset diffs back to the default:

```jsonc
"workbench.diffEditorAssociations": {
  "*.md": "default"
}
```

This is the wrong default. Every custom editor that provides a normal editor would require users to reset the diff association. It should be **opt-in**: a custom editor should be used for diffs/merges only if it explicitly says so.

### Proposal

Introduce a `never` editor priority and make diff/merge opt-in for custom editors.

**1. New `never` priority**

Add `RegisteredEditorPriority.never` (and `CustomEditorPriority.never`). Priorities are resolved per input type — normal editor, diff editor, and merge editor — and `never` for a given input type means:

- The editor is **never** auto-selected for that input type (normal, diff, or merge).
- It is **skipped** for that input type even when a general `workbench.editorAssociations` entry points at it.
- It can still be reached explicitly via `Reopen Editor With…`, or forced by the specialized `workbench.diffEditorAssociations` / merge association.

**2. Diff/merge opt out by default for custom editors**

Resolve the `customEditors` contribution point priority per input type:

- `priority: "default"` (or any string) expands to `{ textEditor: <value>, diff: never, merge: never }`.
- Omitting `priority` yields `{ textEditor: option, diff: never, merge: never }`.
- `diffEditor` / `mergeEditor` no longer inherit from `textEditor`; they default to `never` and must be set explicitly (behind the `customEditorPriority` API proposal) for the editor to participate in diffs/merges.

**3. Resolution respects `never`**

The "which user association may select an editor" step filters out general `editorAssociations` entries whose editor is `never` for the requested input type. The specialized `diffEditorAssociations` setting is still allowed to force a `never` editor, since choosing it is an explicit, diff-scoped decision.

### Behavior summary

| Setting | Normal editor | Diff / merge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.editor` | Markdown editor | **Text diff editor** (was: Markdown side-by-side) — `vscode.markdown.editor` has `diffEditor: never` |
| `editorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.preview.editor` | Markdown Preview | Markdown Preview — this editor opts in with `diffEditor: option`, so the association applies to diffs too |
| `diffEditorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.editor` | (unchanged) | Markdown editor (forced) |
| Custom editor declares `priority.diffEditor: default` | per `textEditor` | Custom editor participates in diffs |

### Compatibility

- Custom editors that only provide a normal editor no longer need users to reset `diffEditorAssociations`.
- **Breaking for extensions relying on implicit diff registration:** an extension that registers a default editor is currently used for diffs automatically. With the priority mechanism, diff/merge default to `never`, so such extensions must now **explicitly opt in** via `priority.diffEditor` / `priority.mergeEditor` to keep participating in diffs/merges. A registration-time warning can flag editors that provide a diff factory without opting in.
- Existing resolver-level string priorities (used by built-in registrations via `toRegisteredEditorPriorityInfo`) still expand to all-equal priorities, so built-in diff behavior is unaffected.

---

Additionally, there is https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324795 to make it easier to discover/switch to custom editors.

### Verification steps

1. Add to `settings.json`:
   ```jsonc
   "workbench.editorAssociations": {
     "*.md": "vscode.markdown.editor"
   }
   ```
2. Open a `*.md` file — it opens in the Markdown custom editor. ✅ (association still applies to the normal editor)
3. Open a diff of a `*.md` file (e.g. from the SCM view or `git.openChange`) — it opens in the **text diff editor**, not the Markdown editor side-by-side. ✅ (custom editor opts out of diffs by default; no `diffEditorAssociations` reset needed)
4. Now add:
   ```jsonc
   "workbench.diffEditorAssociations": {
     "*.md": "vscode.markdown.editor"
   }
   ```
   Re-open the `*.md` diff — it now uses the Markdown editor. ✅ (specialized diff association forces the `never` editor)
5. Remove the diff association again and use **Reopen Editor With…** on a `*.md` diff — the Markdown editor is still offered and works when picked. ✅ (`never` only blocks automatic/association selection, not explicit choice)
6. Sanity check an exclusive custom editor (e.g. the Hex editor): its behavior is unchanged.

Introduce a `never` editor priority and make diff/merge opt-in for custom editors.

**1. New `never` priority**

Add `RegisteredEditorPriority.never` (and `CustomEditorPriority.never`). Priorities are resolved per input type — normal editor, diff editor, and merge editor — and `never` for a given input type means:

- The editor is **never** auto-selected for that input type (normal, diff, or merge).
- It is **skipped** for that input type even when a general `workbench.editorAssociations` entry points at it.
- It can still be reached explicitly via `Reopen Editor With…`, or forced by the specialized `workbench.diffEditorAssociations` / merge association.

**2. Diff/merge opt out by default for custom editors**

Resolve the `customEditors` contribution point priority per input type:

- `priority: "default"` (or any string) expands to `{ textEditor: <value>, diff: never, merge: never }`.
- Omitting `priority` yields `{ textEditor: option, diff: never, merge: never }`.
- `diffEditor` / `mergeEditor` no longer inherit from `textEditor`; they default to `never` and must be set explicitly (behind the `customEditorPriority` API proposal) for the editor to participate in diffs/merges.

**3. Resolution respects `never`**

The "which user association may select an editor" step filters out general `editorAssociations` entries whose editor is `never` for the requested input type. The specialized `diffEditorAssociations` setting is still allowed to force a `never` editor, since choosing it is an explicit, diff-scoped decision.

### Behavior summary

| Setting | Normal editor | Diff / merge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.editor` | Markdown editor | **Text diff editor** (was: Markdown side-by-side) — `vscode.markdown.editor` has `diffEditor: never` |
| `editorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.preview.editor` | Markdown Preview | Markdown Preview — this editor opts in with `diffEditor: option`, so the association applies to diffs too |
| `diffEditorAssociations: *.md → vscode.markdown.editor` | (unchanged) | Markdown editor (forced) |
| Custom editor declares `priority.diffEditor: default` | per `textEditor` | Custom editor participates in diffs |

### Compatibility

- Custom editors that only provide a normal editor no longer need users to reset `diffEditorAssociations`.
- **Breaking for extensions relying on implicit diff registration:** an extension that registers a default editor is currently used for diffs automatically. With the priority mechanism, diff/merge default to `never`, so such extensions must now **explicitly opt in** via `priority.diffEditor` / `priority.mergeEditor` to keep participating in diffs/merges. A registration-time warning can flag editors that provide a diff factory without opting in.
- Existing resolver-level string priorities (used by built-in registrations via `toRegisteredEditorPriorityInfo`) still expand to all-equal priorities, so built-in diff behavior is unaffected.

---

Additionally, there is https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324795 to make it easier to discover/switch to custom editors.

1. Add to `settings.json`:
   ```jsonc
   "workbench.editorAssociations": {
     "*.md": "vscode.markdown.editor"
   }
   ```
2. Open a `*.md` file — it opens in the Markdown custom editor. ✅ (association still applies to the normal editor)
3. Open a diff of a `*.md` file (e.g. from the SCM view or `git.openChange`) — it opens in the **text diff editor**, not the Markdown editor side-by-side. ✅ (custom editor opts out of diffs by default; no `diffEditorAssociations` reset needed)
4. Now add:
   ```jsonc

   Re-open the `*.md` diff — it now uses the Markdown editor. ✅ (specialized diff association forces the `never` editor)

title: Integrated browser: auto-reload HTML files on change
description:
When I open an HTML file in the integrated browser and then edit it, the preview does not refresh automatically — I have to manually hit reload every time. A live-reload / watch-on-change behavior would remove a lot of tiny repetitive clicks.

### Steps to reproduce
1. Open an HTML file in the integrated browser
2. Edit the HTML file and save
3. Notice the browser preview still shows the old content
4. Manually reload to see the change (repeat on every edit)

### Expected
The integrated browser preview auto-reloads when the underlying HTML file changes (ideally automatic for local HTML previews, or an opt-in toggle).

title: Support line range syntax in Quick Open (Go to File)
description:
### Feature request

In Quick Open (**Go to File**), you can type a file path followed by `:<line>` or `:<line>:<column>` to open a file at a specific position. It would be useful to also support a **line range** using a hyphen, so that pressing Enter opens the file with that range selected.

### Proposed syntax

- `file.txt:20-40` → select from the start of line 20 to the start of line 40
- `file.txt:20:3-40:5` → select from line 20, col 3 to line 40, col 5
- `file.txt:20:3-40` → end column defaults to the start of the end line
- Should also work with the existing separator/style variants: `file.txt#20#3-40,5`, `file.txt(20,3-40,5)`

This mirrors the range syntax VS Code already uses for markdown document links (`#L10-L20`), so a bare `10-20` selects from the start of line 10 to the start of line 20.

### Notes

- The parsing lives in `extractRangeFromFilter` (`src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/common/search.ts`), which is reached through the file picker (`AnythingQuickAccessProvider`).

Addressed by [#324318](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/324318).

(Written by Copilot)

title: When utility small model is not selected, Copilot fails to use BYOK provider
description:
related to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/322751: Idea is good, but implementation is flawed: currently if no utility model selected, Copilot just fails to respond, showing the error

> No utility model is configured for 'copilot-utility-small' while the selected main model is BYOK.

Moreover, I'm using llama.cpp with the model fitted tightly to VRAM, so re-loading the model is much higher overhead than just using the currently selected one for small requests. But if I have Qwen3.6 selected, and my utility model is, for example, Gemma 4 12B, its usage will require re-loading the model. To avoid that, there should be an option "Use same model as the main selected one", and a way to select models of a different provider (currently, dropdowns for utility models only list models of the BYOK provider).

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: builtin to VS Code
- VS Code Version: 1.128.0-insider (7e7f9505b9ef0a7a0899794997d4b1cb608084fc)
- OS Version: 10.0.26200.8655
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): BYOK
- Logs:
```
2026-07-02 11:48:59.653 [warning] [IntentDetector] Skipping participant detection context telemetry: No utility model is configured for 'copilot-utility-small' while the selected main model is BYOK.
2026-07-02 11:48:59.712 [warning] [virtual-tools] Had to drop 1 tools due to limit constraints
2026-07-02 11:48:59.713 [warning] [virtual-tools] Had to drop 1 tools due to limit constraints
2026-07-02 11:48:59.722 [error] Error: No utility model is configured for 'copilot-utility-small' while the selected main model is BYOK.
	at f_._resolveUtilityFamily (/home/user/.vscode-server-insiders/bin/7e7f9505b9ef0a7a0899794997d4b1cb608084fc/extensions/copilot/dist/extension.js:6873:16909)
2026-07-02 11:49:00.811 [info] message 0 returned. finish reason: [stop]
2026-07-02 11:49:00.813 [info] request done: requestId: [fe717424-7a8a-439a-aaca-82bc4bc7f0d0] model deployment ID: []
2026-07-02 11:49:00.814 [info] ccreq:ade8e125.copilotmd | success | gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 | 679ms | [title]
```

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Configure `chatLanguageModels.json` to include
```
	{
		"name": "llama.cpp@:8080",
		"vendor": "customendpoint",
		"apiType": "chat-completions",
		"models": [
    {
        "id": "qwen3.6-reap-moe-256k",
        "name": "Qwen3.6-28B-REAP20-A3B-256k",
        "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/",
        "toolCalling": true,
        "vision": true,
        "maxInputTokens": 229376,
        "maxOutputTokens": 32768
    },
    {
        "id": "gemma4-12b-256k",
        "name": "unsloth_gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF:Q6_K_XL-256k",
        "url": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/",
        "toolCalling": true,
        "vision": true,
        "maxInputTokens": 229376,
        "maxOutputTokens": 32768
    },
]
```
2. Open Agentic panel, select Qwen3.6-28B-REAP20-A3B-256k
3. Say "Hi", Enter

you'll get the error

> No utility model is configured for 'copilot-utility-small' while the selected main model is BYOK.

4. Configure `unsloth_gemma-4-12b-it-GGUF:Q6_K_XL-256k` in vscode-insiders://settings/chat.utilitySmallModel
5. Retry the response

You'll see the local engine will load the second model (along with the first one if limit permits, or will unload the first model) for the utility use, then switch back to the first model, which is much slower than just generating everything with the same main model.

You may ask, why would I select qwen while gemma is configured as the utility? I frequently switch between models, including a few of my BYOK and models provided by Copilot.

The previous behavior of always using copilot models for utility worked for me mostly, but it is flawed in some parts and for example prevented me from ever using commit message generation with copilot. Also it fails when internet connectivity is missing. This in an opportunity to fix both issues!

Also perhaps, the utility model should be configurable per provider in `chatLanguageModels.json`, with same options as available in the user `settings.json`, so a cloud BYOK configuration allow setting up different `chat.utilityModel` and `chat.utilitySmallModel`, while llama.cpp config having `main` there (or some other non-model-name keyword) to avoid re-loading.

Either way, utility models should not be restricted to the same provider as the main selected model.

title: Session header meta row with consistent pills and clickable diff/changes
description:
The Agents window **session header meta row** (the row under the title) has been reworked so contributed actions render consistently as compact secondary-button **pills**, and the diff/changes affordance is clickable and accurate.

## What shipped

- **Unified meta row** — workspace, changes, and pull request actions all render through `Menus.SessionHeaderMeta` as uniform secondary-button pills.
- **Workspace folder pill** — the workspace label is now a leading "Open Files" pill showing the workspace icon (cloud / folder / worktree per workspace kind) + label, with truncation for long names. Its hover shows the repo folder and working directory on separate lines, plus the git branch. The branch name was removed from the header title.
- **Changes / diff-stats pill** — a clickable `⊟ N files +X -Y` pill that opens the multi-file diff editor, reading and opening the session's default changeset (correct for both Copilot and agent-host providers).

title: Make it easier to switch between browsers and editors
description:
Feedback from accessibility sync:

In the current UI model, where editors and browser tabs are mixed together, it's difficult to quickly switch between the "edit" and "verify" flows compared to an external browser where you can easily go back and forth with e.g. `Alt+Tab`.

Potential solutions:
- Add a setting to always open browser tabs in a particular location -- e.g. the current editor group (same as today), a dedicated side group (locked from other editors), or a new window.
- (Preferred) have a dedicated panel for browsers, like terminal does today. Then have a shortcut akin to `` Ctrl+` `` to quickly toggle that panel.

title: Support Multi-Chat in Claude harness
description:
Summary

Add Multi-Chat support to the Claude harness so it matches the Copilot experience.

Background

- The Multi-Chat feature (previously called Sub-Sessions) is currently available for the Copilot harness and works in AHP sessions for Copilot.
- Team feedback and user studies have shown confusion around the feature and its name; the UX should be consistent across harnesses rather than Copilot-only.
- Claude AHP sessions do not currently show the Multi-Chat UI.

Proposal

- Implement Multi-Chat in the Claude harness with parity to the Copilot implementation and UX.
- Ensure Multi-Chat is available in AHP sessions for Claude as it is for Copilot.
- Minimize agent integration effort (sessions should be transparent to agents where possible), and document any agent-facing changes required.
- Update tests, e2e scenarios, and relevant documentation to reflect Multi-Chat availability in the Claude harness.

Acceptance criteria

- Multi-Chat UI appears and behaves the same in the Claude harness as it does in Copilot.
- Multi-Chat is available and functional in AHP sessions for Claude.
- Agent/handler code for Claude either requires no changes or any required changes are documented and minimal.
- Relevant tests and documentation updated.

Implementation notes

- Verify whether sessions need to be linked or if the agent surface can remain unchanged (transparent sessions).
- Coordinate UX changes with the Copilot harness team to ensure consistency and avoid repeating prior confusion around naming/behavior.
- Add testing steps to validate in manual and automated tests across the Claude harness and AHP sessions.

---

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
**Problem**
There's currently no easy way to copy a code block from the rendered Markdown preview — you have to manually select the text, which is fiddly and easy to get wrong (e.g. accidentally including line numbers or surrounding text).

**Proposal**
Add a hover-triggered copy icon/button on each fenced code block (` ``` `) in the Markdown preview, similar to how GitHub, GitLab, and most documentation sites handle it. Clicking it copies the raw code content to the clipboard.

**Scope**
This applies specifically to the built-in **Markdown preview** (`markdown-language-features` extension) — not the Markdown source editor itself.

**Additional context**
Happy to put together a prototype/PR for this if the team is open to it.

title: Deprecate built-in chat "Edit" mode
description:
## Summary

Edit mode (`ChatModeKind.Edit`) is one of the three built-in chat modes (Ask / Edit / Agent). It is already in a "deprecated but supported" state:

- The mode picker only surfaces Edit when Agent mode is disabled by enterprise policy.
- The setting `chat.editMode.hidden` (default `true`, policy `DeprecatedEditModeHidden`) is now vestigial — it is read in only one place (`chatNewActions.ts`), and the mode picker doesn't read it at all (it uses `agentModeDisabledViaPolicy`).

This issue tracks **fully removing `chat.editMode.hidden` and not allowing Edit to be selected from the agent dropdown**.

Ref https://code.visualstudio.com/updates/v1_110#_new-deprecations-in-this-release

## Design notes

- When Agent is disabled by enterprise policy, the picker can still fallback to the Edit experience.
